comments.text: Jump to the music initializer at $6C87. A selects an eight-byte song header at $77E5; this load provides two headers.
Jump to the per-update music driver at $6CEC. This copy updates two SID voices, preserving the third for the resident effect driver.

Jump into the initializer's three-byte fade-state reset. A is stored in $6C13-$6C15 and starts a fade: the camera routine at $EA46 passes six when the camera column word has a nonzero high byte, low byte $C0 and the fine scroll is three; the boss passes five at $8958 when its last stage ends; and the resident calls at $4F44 and $53EB pass five.

Increment the music stop flag through $6DF2. While that flag remains set, later play calls write its value (one after a single stop) to all three SID control registers, which selects no waveform, and to the three fade-state bytes at $6C13-$6C15.
Current voice index, saved while helpers temporarily use X. The adjacent byte at $6C0D preserves an effect-record offset during pulse/filter modulation.

A nonzero value diverts each play call to $6CD9, which writes the flag's value to the three SID control registers and to the fade-state bytes at $6C13-$6C15 and returns. The initializer clears it; the stop entry and the end of an order list increment it at $6DF2.

Multiply A by eight and read the selected song header. Set tick speeds, three order pointers and initial note durations; clear order/pattern positions, effect state and stop flags. Set volume fifteen and clear all three SID control registers. Fall through to the fade-state reset.
Store A into the three consecutive fade-state bytes and return. Initialization reaches here with A zero; the separate entry at $6C06 permits a caller-selected value.
Store A into the fade reload at $6C14 and active fade tick at $6C15, then return. Order commands enter here to change or clear the fade without replacing the separate parameter at $6C13.

If stopped, write the stop flag's value to all three SID controls and the three fade-state bytes, and return. Otherwise clear decimal mode, update fade and tick dividers, then process voices one and zero. Expired note durations parse order and pattern streams; other updates apply waveform, pitch, pulse and filter effects. Finish by writing the shared filter cutoff and mode/volume registers.

Save X as the active voice. If its duration is nonzero, update the current instrument effects. Otherwise clear per-note effect state, turn off the existing gate and parse its order stream at the saved position.

Interpret order bytes: $FF reads a byte-position loop target; $80-$BF set transposition; $C0-$DF set the instrument addend; $E0-$FA set pattern repeats. $FB replaces the tick speeds. While the fade parameter at $6C13 is zero, $FC clears the fade reload and tick and restores volume fifteen, and $FD stores its following byte as the fade reload and tick; with a nonzero parameter both leave the fade alone, and $FD still passes over its byte. $FE reaches the stop entry. A nonnegative byte selects a pattern through $78E3/$78FC.
Increment the stop flag and return. Subsequent play calls take the stop branch, which writes the flag's value to all three voice controls, selecting no waveform, and to the three fade-state bytes.

Select the pattern pointer and saved position. Commands set durations, release overrides, instrument/arpeggio selectors, filter/pulse freeze state or slide parameters. Notes below $60 apply order transposition; bytes $60-$7F select a rest duration. A following $FF ends/repeats the pattern and advances its order position when the repeat count expires.

Convert the selected note to frequency, load its instrument control, attack/decay and sustain/release, initialize pulse width unless frozen, and initialize shared filter parameters unless globally frozen. Write envelope registers and enter the normal SID control/output path.

Apply flagged direct high-frequency or age-derived pitch updates; a successful update skips the target-slide/vibrato branch. Otherwise run an eligible target slide or vibrato. Then process per-voice pulse modulation, shared filter modulation, arpeggio and waveform/pitch streams, in that order. Gate-timing flags can force early release or noise/reset control before output.
Select the voice's seven-register offset and write control, pulse width and frequency. Iterate to the next lower voice index, then write the shared filter cutoff and mode/volume.

Select waveform and pitch sequence pointers from the instrument's waveform mode. $FF reads a sequence loop position, $FE holds, and the pitch sequence's $FD advances then restores the base note frequency. Other pitch entries replace the frequency high byte and clear its low byte.
Operand byte 1 of the LDY instruction at $7139, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.
Follow the selected signed note-offset stream, holding on $80 and jumping to a byte index on $81. Add the current note number and look up its resulting frequency.
Use Y as a note-table index and copy low/high frequency bytes from $73FE/$745E into the active voice's frequency state.

Multiply the slide magnitude by four to form a sixteen-bit frequency step. Add or subtract toward the target note frequency; clamp when it crosses the target, then clear slide/vibrato state and make the target the current note.

On first use compute a frequency difference from an instrument-selected note offset and right-shift it by the selected scale. Later age bounds can adjust that step. Reset to the base note, read the signed multiplier stream and repeatedly add/subtract the step; $81 jumps to a stream index and zero holds the frequency.

Unless frozen for X, clear the modulation stream position and hold count and load its initial direction from bit two of the selected effect record. X zero through two select pulse width; X three selects the shared filter cutoff.

Read an optional modulation stream with loop, hold and repeat commands, or apply the record's constant steps: one word added while rising, another subtracted while falling. Compare against its upper/lower bounds; bit zero of the record's flag byte for that bound stops the modulation, bit one wraps to the opposite bound, and otherwise the direction reverses. Pulse-width and filter cutoff share this implementation through four state slots.

Vibrato stream, ten bytes. The three vibrato records point at it (their pointers at $7726, $772E, $7736), and update_music_vibrato reads it at $7283, one entry a pass: a positive entry adds the record's step to the frequency that many times (0, 1, 2, 1, 0), a negative one takes it away ($FF once, $FE twice, $FF once), and $81 is followed by the position to go back to, here $00. So the pitch rises and falls in a cycle of eight passes. The pulse and filter code reads its sixteen-byte records through bases from $7736 to $7745, with Y a nonzero multiple of sixteen, so instructions such as lda $773D,y name addresses here without reading these bytes.

Actor type three selects one of ten colours, shapes, health values and death scores. Initialize its movement fields and set the recorded weapon-hit index to the negative $D3 sentinel. Updates accept invulnerable player contact or a nonnegative weapon-hit index through $A1C1. The variants implement curved leftward flight, fixed-direction firing, a facing-selected four-half-pixel projectile, two curve paths, downward motion and fast leftward motion. Bounds or terrain can release a variant.

A nonnegative $BC10,X value is a flight weapon damage index. Reset it to $D3, subtract the selected amount from actor health and flash with the subtype-specific colour on survival. Health underflow, invulnerable contact or the common kill flag awards the subtype's score and selects explosion state.

Variant zero cycles three frames, moves left and follows an eighteen-entry Y curve with terrain checks. Variants one through four periodically emit directed type-sixteen projectiles. Variant five moves horizontally according to its saved facing flag. Variants six and seven follow fifty-entry curves while firing timer-spaced shots; eight moves down two pixels and nine moves left six half-pixels until terrain or bounds remove it.

Actor type four reserves a vertically adjacent partner, gives the controller thirty-two health and a sixty-four-update initial firing delay, and sets both weapon-hit flags to $D3. It approaches the player's horizontal vicinity and follows the player's lower Y span. Every thirty-three updates it emits a type-three variant-five projectile, using its facing to select the offset and show a short firing pose. Death awards 1000 points and explodes both components.

Actor type five has two subtype paths. The original has twelve health and changes colour through a sixty-four-entry table; a hit that takes its health below zero, or contact with the invulnerable player, attempts to spawn two subtype-one children before exploding, and the common kill flag explodes it without them.
